text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Under a Federal Government reform blueprint for Australian shipping, which could trigger a major industrial dispute with maritime unions, the industry could be opened up to foreign competition and union members forced to accept cuts in employment entitlemnts or face losing their jobs. The radical overhaul is outlined in a report delivered yesterday to Transport Minister John Sharp by Perkins Shipping chief executive Julian Manser. Page 1.

Last-minute moves by the Federal Government to drop controversial clause 34 of the superannuation surcharge, which top lawyer Dennis Rose QC claimed was unconstitutional, have opened the possibility that employer-sponsored super funds may be hit with the surcharge, throwing the super industry into confusion. Page 3.

Telecommunications service providers, which are expected to provide new competition to Optus and Telstra, have generally reacted positively to the Federal Government's massive telecommunications reform package, passed by the Senate on Monday night. Page 5.

In a decision that will further delay Telstra's plan to cut 22,000 jobs over the next three years under its controversial "Resource Rebalancing" proposal, the Australian Industrial Relations Commission ruled yesterday that elements of the plan would be harsh and unjust to employees. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In an Oscars ceremony otherwise dominated by The English Patient, which received nine awards, Australian actor Geoffrey Rush won the award for best actor last night for his portrayal of pianist David Helfgott's troubled life. Rush used his acceptance speech to hit back at critics who called Helfgott's US tour a circus. Page 1.

Euthanasia doctor Philip Nitschke revealed last night one of his terminally ill patients may seek to die under the Northern Territory's controversial euthanasia law before assent is given to the Federal legislation passed yesterday which overturns the world-first right-to-die legislation. Assent by Governor-General Sir William Deane is expected before Easter. Page 1.

In a unique, multi-million dollar deal described by Australian Olympic officials as "historic", News Limited and John Fairfax Holdings, Australia's two biggest newspaper publishers, yesterday became the first publishers to become top-flight sponsors of th Sydney 2000 Olympic Games. Page 1.

Speaking yesterday after being appointed as the new chair of the Australia Council, Margaret Seares acknowledged she has taken one of Australia's toughest arts jobs, saying one of the biggest challenges is balancing the Council's many competing sectors, while cultivating new work. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The States are allowing thousands of public servants to escape tax on their superannuation payments by refusing to co-operate with the Federal Government on the implementation of its super surcharge. The States have warned they will not legislate to overcome the constitutional difficulties in applying the tax, and the Federal Government has retaliated by shelving a proposed change to the High Court legislation allowing the States more input. Page 1.

Forty-five-year old Geoffrey Rush's portrayal of pianist David Helfgott in Shine has won him the Oscar for Best Actor at the 1997 Academy Awards in America yesterday. Rush, who has won virtually all major film acting honours, achieved the only victory ou of seven nominations for Shine. Page 1.

In the two years since the NT's right to die legislation was passed, pro-euthanasia doctor Philip Nitschke has received 60 requests from patients who want help to end their lives. In the wake of the passing of the Andrews Bill yesterday, Nitschke announced he was preparing a study of the characteristics of the patients, most of which were women. Page 1.

Australia has been advised by Indonesia to open private talks with Jakarta in an effort to formulate a joint response to the possible 'systemic collapse' of the Papua New Guinean Government. A senior Indonesian source revealed the informal approach was mde last week in Canberra, as any joint talks would be outside Indonesia's official non-interference policy for the domestic politics of its neighbouring countries. Page 1.
THE AGE

Australian actor Geoffrey Rush added to his collection of film acting honours for his acclaimed performance in Shine, winning the Academy Award for best actor. Rush, 45, won the award for his portrayal of pianist David Helfgott and is the first Australianto win it since Peter Finch, who died before he could accept it in 1977. Page 1.

Amid strong reaction to Federal Parliament's passage of the Andrews private member's Bill yesterday which overturns the Northern Territory's right-to-die law, controversial euthanasia advocate Philip Nitschke confirmed last night one of his two patients panning to use the law may proceed within the next two days to avoid acting outside the now-overturned law. Page 1.

As the number of people affected by Victoria's latest food poisoning outbreak reached 370 yesterday, including 25 requiring hospital treatment, State chief health officer Graham Rouch revealed a strain of salmonella commonly found in livestock and mice - nown as typhimurium - has been identified as the source. Page 1.

Victorian Advocacy League for Individuals with Disability executive director Kevin Stone yesterday said Kew Cottages should be closed following research revealing that intellectually disabled people are better off in the community than in institutions. To study reports on the relocation of former residents of Caloola, Arandale and Mayday Hills training centres were launched yesterday by Victorian Human Services Minister Denis Napthine. Page 2.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
